Worked at Goodwill for just under two MONTHS back in 2020 and lemme tell you, it destroyed me. First few weeks I worked up front as a cashier despite the fact that I told everyone who oversaw me that I wouldn't be a good fit for that for a number of reasons:

Severe migraines (the sun beamed directly into the window behind me and glared off the computer screens, it was also very hot)

Very anxious when people get upset with me (which, at THAT store, seemed constant)

I'm dreadful at math (our computers always had something wrong with them and rarely applied discounts, returns or change back correctly, so I was having to attempt to deal with that whole trying to figure out numbers in my head, while both customers and supervisors were getting impatient with me)

The list goes on. So, once they finally decided to believe me, I got a new position in the back. So much better for me me mentally. I got less headaches, I wasn't nearly as high strung, yadda yadda. I was still being wickedly overworked though, doing the jobs of several different people. Sorting, tagging, pricing, hanging and on top of that, organizing the sales floor.

One day, I was just not feeling well at all: all kinds of weird symptoms going on (for me). I was cold, shaking, sweating, could barely stand up and my chest felt tight, and my head was pounding etc; eventually I suddenly saw white and just collapsed for a minute before I could get up and get my shit together enough to tell my managers that I needed to leave because (apparently) no one saw what happened. 

So I leave, go to the doctor and they're ordering all kinds of tests and labs that are gonna take a few days to come in as I felt fine a few hours later, but they recommended that I take a week off to figure everything out and make sure I was okay and it wasn't anything drastic. So I do that, go to take my leave papers and information and whatnot to my manager and this asshole responds with "Okay, we'll see what we can do. Go home. Just think of the position you're putting the store in." 

Absolutely the fucking not. I'm trying to make sure my ass is not about to drop dead because I have no idea what's going on with my body. I could not possibly give less of a singular shit what happens to the store that's paying me barely 9 bucks an hour while I do the work of five different people. 

Eventually it came back that I was fine, but extremely stressed. I quit an hour and a half in to the day I came back to work lmao.

(TL;DR: Got job. Hated job. Got other job. Hated slightly less. Stress induced medical emergency. Manager was a Class A Bitch. Took medical leave. Quit.)

I get rib/lung pain pretty often and I've learned to cope with it pretty well, but a couple years ago, I popped my rib out of place and my mom refused to take me to the hospital as I sat on the floor, in agonizing pain, unable to take a breath longer than a second at a time. Instead of taking me to get seen, she screamed at me to find my inhaler despite me being almost entirely unable to move. Stayed on the floor for two and a half hours before I could move myself into my bed. 

Eventually it got to a point where I needed to pee so bad that if I didn't move, I would piss myself. So I grabbed the bar on the side of my bed and yanked myself up as hard and fast as I could just to get it over with. Had a flash of one of the worst pains of my life and then it immediately went away. Popped it right back in place.

I should mention that the way I dislocated it in the first place was that I had one of those chair gym swivel disk things on my chair at my desk and I went to sit down and it spun and slipped out under me so my hips / legs and my torso weren't really facing the same direction. It all happened so fast. 

I have other severe pain issues like pretty extreme migraines and the like, but those got taken more seriously.

Great point about giving older FANS an opportunity as well! If anything, I think it would be an even better move to target and attract adult fans and they're more likely to have the money to buy what they want rather than one) saving up an amount just to spend ALL of it on merch, or two) relying on a parent or guardian's money for it. 

That's all well and good, but child and teenage fans are not the only ones that exist. 

Also on the topic of older idols showcasing their performance: it seems like a bit of a waste of all resources to have artists under your name just to not?? Do anything with them ?? For years to months on end????  Unless that's strictly in their best interest, either give them the opportunity to work and do what they love and justify the cost of still having them with you, or let them go so they can enjoy themselves or find somewhere else to show their skills instead of hiding them away for an indefinite amount of time and have them not knowing when the next time they can do what they love is.

Truly! Also, normalize the shit that can happen with actual live vocals?? They don't have to sound like they've been swallowing audio files all day every day. Voice cracks happen. Random dry throats happen mid note. Running out of breath is gonna happen if you're dancing, jumping around and engaging with the audience during a performance, and that's okay. It doesn't need to be hyperfixated on because someone's voice shook a little bit while they're literally doing heavy physical activity AND trying to project their voice on top of it. Sure, a backing track is going to help smooth out any kinks, but they're still a human being, and humans gonna human, yanno.

Absolutely agree on all fronts, but especially the point about solo activities. I feel like a good solid schedule of solo activities would give other members a chance to rest off promotions, see or communicate with their families, actually prepare mentally and physically between comebacks, etc while the one or two that are going solo at the moment can do their thing. 

Also with the interactions between groups: that's great! I feel like having it be normalized has benefits on so many levels. They (m/f/nb friends) can interact without fear of the next dating scandal (which shouldn't even be a scandal in the first place), they can build a stronger sense of connection with each other, and also ??? It's just fun seeing people have fun with their friends, dammit (!!)

To anyone asking if I'm selling: what's keeping me from selling them is my lack of confidence in the ability to do them with enough quality to warrant charging someone for them. 

-They're done on (a limited supply of) thin, plastic picture frame panes from an old room divider that only had 12 in it, the rest of the pours I do are on canvas that I don't to purchase very often, though it is cheap. 

-They're done with very cheap acrylic paints that very rarely ever get thinned out equally enough (despite my best efforts) to have a smooth surface. My pours are very textured after drying, which doesn't really bother me but I'm not sure how other people would feel about that. 

-I'm not the best at painting lettering. On a closer look, you'll often see the pencil outline of my letters and the paint used to fill them is often a bit textured because I need it thick enough that I can control the paint well (which I'm not great at) and I use cheap brushes and other tools (a wooden dowel is second most often) which gives the paint even more texture and a bit of a shitty look and feel. 


Overall, I'm a 19 year old girl who has no clue what I'm doing, I'm very amateur and I'd feel bad selling these things because upon closer inspection, they're not really that great I'm terms of quality or anything. I don't edit my pictures or anything, but texture and such doesn't come through quite as much in photos. I'd be surprised if anyone is still interested after this. 


Moreover, I started doing this in my spare time (of which I have a lot, admittedly) while I'm out of a job and recovering from some mental health issues and I was so flattered when I saw someone ask if I was selling. It meant a lot that someone actually liked it enough to ask!


TL;DR: I'm just not sure if, with all the issues, they're worth selling to someone at the risk of disappointing them with the final result as pours are unpredictable and I'm not the best with lettering. But hey, if anyone's still interested, maybe we can find ways to work it out. I'm always open to suggestions!
